title: Why Drain Traps Dry Out and Cause Sewer Gas Odors
description: Sewer gas escaping into a building is often caused by a compromised trap seal in the drainage system. A P-trap relies on a continuous water barrier to block harmful gases. When a fixture goes unused for long periods, standing water evaporates. Alternatively, improper venting can create negative air pressure during drainage, siphoning water out of the trap. Identifying whether gas leaks stem from evaporation or siphoning helps plumbers diagnose venting defects and restore proper seal integrity quickly.

Why Drain Traps Dry Out and Cause Sewer Gas Odors

Sewer gas escaping into a building is often caused by a compromised trap seal in the drainage system. A P-trap relies on a continuous water barrier to block harmful gases. When a fixture goes unused for long periods, standing water evaporates. Alternatively, improper venting can create negative air pressure during drainage, siphoning water out of the trap. Identifying whether gas leaks stem from evaporation or siphoning helps plumbers diagnose venting defects and restore proper seal integrity quickly.
